summary: This paper proposes the Hierarchical Logical Processor (HLP), which concatenates a high-rate quantum CSS code with the rotated surface code (RSC) to achieve improved qubit efficiency while requiring long-range gates only once every $\Theta(d_0)$ syndrome extraction rounds. The key innovation is the shuttle bus—an elongated RSC patch enabling transversal hybrid-unit CNOT gates to couple multiple data qubits simultaneously, supporting efficient parallel logical measurements while maintaining suppressed error correlations.
motivation: Quantum low-density parity-check codes offer high encoding efficiency but require frequent non-local couplings that introduce additional errors and implementation complexity. Platforms like neutral atom arrays support long-range connectivity but incur overhead; reducing the frequency of such operations while retaining encoding gains is essential for practical fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The HLP concatenates a distance-$d_1$ CSS code at level 1 with distance-$d_0$ RSC patches (cores) at level 0, introducing elongated RSC patches (shuttle buses) of width $d_0$ and length $d_0 d_1$. Transversal hybrid-unit CNOT gates between shuttle buses and cores enable efficient readout gadgets for level-1 syndrome extraction and logical Pauli measurements. Circuit-level simulations employ correlated matching for level-0 decoding and soft-output extraction to compute level-1 error probabilities.
result: At a physical error rate of $10^{-3}$, an HLP based on the $[[256,194,4]]$ code achieves 3–4× higher qubit efficiency than standard RSC. Compared to the yoked surface code, this HLP reduces space overhead per logical qubit by 100–200 physical qubits and shortens the level-1 syndrome extraction cycle by a factor of 20–30. Theoretical analysis proves that with compilation parameters $\alpha_\mathsf{b} = d_1$ and $\alpha_\mathsf{c} = 1$, level-1 errors are approximately local stochastic with effective error rate $\sim p^{d_0/2}$, achieving beyond-RSC encoding efficiency.
